sections.h2: Where the Surry County tax office is
sections.html:
The Tax Department is at the Surry County Service Center, 915 East Atkins Street, Dobson, NC 27017, phone (336) 401-8100. It opens weekdays 8:15 to 5:00. Dobson is the county seat, and the tax and records offices are both there.

Surry County Tax Department contact points

Assessment mailP.O. Box 588
Collections mailP.O. Box 576
Pay in personDrive-thru window at the same address
Fax(336) 401-8120

An online taxpayer portal also handles bill searches. The appraisal office fax is (336) 401-8147, and the use value desk uses (336) 401-8106. Both sit behind the main number, (336) 401-8100.

sections.h2: How Surry County appraises about 44,000 parcels
sections.html:
Appraisers sort the parcels into roughly 370 neighborhoods of similar homes, price land and buildings from sales, check the results in the field and office, then mail notices of value. The commissioners must approve the Schedule of Values, the manual of rates and adjustments, before it applies.

The county defines value as the most probable price in a competitive, open market. Periodic revaluation keeps some owners from paying more than their share while others pay less, which is the county's stated reason for reappraising.

The current revaluation took effect January 1, 2025. In 2017 the commissioners moved the county from the eight-year state maximum to a five-year cycle, producing an effective date of January 1, 2021, and the county now calls itself a four-year county.

Values hold until the next revaluation except for changes to a property. Call the tax office to learn when the next one takes effect.

sections.h2: Where do I take a Surry County value dispute?
sections.html:
Ask the Tax Department for an informal review, or file with the county's special review board. The board has existed since 1982, the commissioners reappoint it each January, and it sits by the first Monday in May.

  • The board can change any value it finds out of line.
  • Each timely appellant may appear.
  • A losing appellant can go on to the state Property Tax Commission.

Bring documents showing why the value differs from market value, or facts about the property that affect it. The Real Estate page of the tax website has a link to submit an informal appeal for real property online, along with the 2025 appraisal manual, the use value manual and the revaluation FAQ.

sections.h2: When Surry County tax goes delinquent
sections.html:
Interest is added to payments made on or after January 6 following the due date: 2% the first month, then 0.75% for each month. The county treats the tax and interest charges as non-negotiable.

Its collection tools are garnishment, bank attachment, seizure of personal property and foreclosure under G.S. 105-365 to 105-368, and remedies on real property must begin within 10 years of the due date. A delinquent real property list is posted on its collections page.

The circuit breaker caps tax at 4.0% of income up to the eligibility limit and 5.0% above it, up to 150% of the limit. The revenue department's 2026 figures are $38,800 and $58,200, and an application is needed every year.

The owner must be 65 or disabled and must have lived in and owned the home for five years. Deferred tax becomes a lien, and three prior years come due when the owner sells, dies or moves out. The other two homestead programs, the elderly or disabled exclusion and the $45,000 disabled veteran exclusion, are filed on AV-9 with the county assessor, and an owner may use only one.

Ask Collections for a payoff before accepting an offer, because the lien on the parcel dates to the listing date and rides along until paid.

If the bill is behind, the county can bring an auction action, with commissioner fees up to 5% of the price. Redemption before confirmation requires all taxes, penalties, interest and costs. Paying at closing is the usual fix, and a cash buyer can take the house with the balance attached and clear it from the price.

sections.h2: How Surry County runs tax foreclosure sales
sections.html:
The county directs private attorneys to start formal foreclosure proceedings under G.S. 105-374 against real property with unpaid tax. Properties listed for sale are being foreclosed under a court judgment, and the sales are not the county selling its own surplus land.

  • Property is sold as is, where is, with no warranties from the county.
  • A 20% deposit is due at the time of sale.
  • The upset bid period is 10 calendar days from the sale.
  • Redemption is possible at any time before confirmation, and redeemed parcels are pulled from the process.

Call (336) 401-8100 for the status of a parcel, and check the court file, since the posted list can lag behind real events.

sections.h2: Present use value for farm or woodland
sections.html:
Land enrolled in a use value program is taxed on what it produces rather than what it would sell for, and the county publishes a use value manual for farm, horticultural and forest land. The Tax Department handles enrollment at its Dobson office.

If you are selling enrolled land, ask the department what happens to the enrollment when ownership changes and whether any deferred tax is due. A buyer who plans to build or subdivide will want that answer before the contract is signed.

sections.h2: Other tax office services useful to a seller
sections.html:
Beyond real estate, the Tax Department handles business personal property, personal property, motor vehicles and present use value. Owners can print a motor vehicle tax receipt through the state's MyDMV portal, request a mailing address change, and send public records requests online.

The department also runs GIS mapping and downloadable data. For a seller, the mapping and parcel data are handy for checking acreage and lines before a buyer's survey. For anything the website leaves open, call (336) 401-8100.

Start with the tax office and work outward. Request a payoff figure from Collections, check whether any relief or use value enrollment is attached to the parcel, and ask the appraisal office whether your assessment looks right before you set a price. Then bring the payoff to your closing attorney, who can pay the current bill and any delinquency from your proceeds.

A cash buyer will usually accept the house with its balance and repairs, and the offer reflects both. If you list on the open market, expect the buyer's attorney to ask for the same payoff figure.

  • Call the Tax Department at the main number and ask Collections for the payoff figure in writing.
  • Check the delinquent real property list on the collections page to see whether your parcel appears.
  • If the assessment looks wrong, ask for an informal review or file with the special review board before you set a price.
  • If the land is enrolled in use value, ask whether deferred tax comes due on the sale.
  • Give the closing attorney the payoff so current and past bills are paid from your proceeds.

A cash sale skips the open-market wait, and the balance is simply taken out of the price at closing.

faqs.q: Where is the Surry County Tax Department?
faqs.a: 915 East Atkins Street, Dobson, NC 27017, open weekdays 8:15 to 5:00.

faqs.q: When does interest start on Surry County property tax?
faqs.a: On payments made on or after January 6, at 2% for the first month and 0.75% each month after.

faqs.q: When did Surry County's current revaluation take effect?
When does Surry County's value review board meet?
faqs.a: It convenes each year by the first Monday in May.

faqs.q: Can I pay Surry County property tax in person?
faqs.a: Yes, at the drive-thru window at 915 East Atkins Street, or through the online portal.
